topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, lecture series context, and key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Origins and drivers of cancer: intrinsic factors, genetics, and environment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer by evaluating how intrinsic biological errors, inherited genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents and cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens can drive malignancy, illustrated by the epidemiology and molecular mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific dietary, environmental, and chemical mutagens cause DNA damage directly or through metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promoters and host contextual factors in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic factors, including tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and tissue developmental stages, contribute to malignancy alongside initial mutations.

topics.label: Methods for determining and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and assess their cancer-causing potential.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer risks, carcinogen evaluation challenges, and closing remarks.
